audit_findings.title: The anchor contains income from a terminated business and a litigation windfall
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.5365 million pre-tax leasing-segment contribution; approximately $1.9886 million after tax using the filed 21.6% effective rate, equal to 5.0% of the $39.5 million anchor and approximately $6.74 per share of base value
audit_findings.mechanism: Non-recurring leasing income is embedded in anchor OE and therefore projected through the explicit forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: $2.2 million of the $2.5 million of leasing income for the fiscal year of 2025 was related to the settlement of outstanding customer litigation.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated normalization error: leasing ended, no leasing income was reported in the first half of 2026, and the 2025 segment contribution principally reflected litigation settlement proceeds. Removing the computed after-tax contribution would reduce the base estimate from about $140.43 to $133.69 per share. It does not reverse the large discount to the $318.17 market price, but a perpetual error equal to about 5% of anchor OE is material to the intrinsic-value and buy-below conclusions.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild 2025 OE with franchising operations only, apply the settlement's actual tax treatment, set the operating perimeter to franchising, and rerun every scenario and the buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may treat customer-funded operating cash as excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Cash bridge $25.8345 million; latest total franchise and software deferred revenue $10.0865 million; complete removal of the cash bridge would reduce base value by $6.59 per share, or 4.7%
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unrestricted cash needed to satisfy franchise-service obligations or normal working capital should not be added as excess cash in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 27, 2025, deferred franchise fee revenue was $7,929,600.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved classification possibility, not a demonstrated dollar-for-dollar liability: deferred revenue does not itself establish restricted cash or an equal future cash outflow. Restricted cash is already excluded from the $25.8345 million bridge. Even the conservative extreme of removing the entire cash addition leaves base value near $133.84 per share and cannot alter the conclusion relative to the $318.17 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile unrestricted cash to restricted balances, deferred-fee servicing costs, operating liquidity requirements and OE working-capital treatment; rerun the bridge only for the portion shown not to be excess.

audit_findings.title: POS modernization may require reinvestment above historical capital spending
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.2103 million of capitalized software in the first six months of 2026, equal to 5.6% of anchor OE and 11.5 times fiscal-2025 property-and-equipment purchases of $0.1923 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Maintenance software development, implementation expense and continuing support costs would reduce OE; execution effects could also alter growth and franchise retention.
audit_findings.evidence: We are pursuing a strategic initiative to modernize our POS platform to address legacy constraints and improve the franchisee and in-store experience.
audit_findings.explanation: The elevated cash investment is demonstrated and was not present in the 2025 anchor, but the record does not separate temporary growth investment from recurring maintenance or quantify remaining implementation and support costs. Consequently, the valuation effect may be material but cannot yet be established. The new monthly software fee could offset some costs, but its economics are also unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the total project budget, remaining commitments, capitalization and amortization schedules, recurring support costs, expected software-fee revenue and maintenance-versus-growth allocation, then rerun OE and growth assumptions.

audit_findings.title: A second non-recurring item contaminates the 2025 anchor in the opposite direction
audit_findings.mechanism: A genuinely non-recurring software-license expense retained in 2025 OE lowers the anchor, forecast OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase was primarily due to an increase in compensation related expenses and a non-recurring expense related to third-party software licenses for franchisees.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that such an expense existed but does not disclose its amount. Fiscal-2025 SG&A increased by $3.4132 million in total, but that increase also included compensation and therefore cannot quantify the software charge. It also remains unresolved whether the expenditure was truly isolated or part of continuing POS modernization. No offset against the separate litigation windfall can be assumed.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the software-license charge from the general ledger or management disclosure, determine whether comparable costs recur, normalize it separately, and rerun all scenarios without netting it informally against leasing income.

audit_findings.title: An accrued tax claim ahead of common equity is absent from the stated bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.8932 million at fiscal 2025 year-end; even deducting the entire latest $2.1658 million other-liabilities balance would equal about $0.55 per share or 0.39% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any tax settlement not already captured in OE cash conversion would reduce excess cash or require a separate equity-bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: The amount of unrecognized tax benefits, including interest and penalties, as of December 27, 2025 and December 28, 2024, was $1,893,200 and $1,663,400, respectively, primarily for potential state taxes.
audit_findings.explanation: The accrued exposure is demonstrated, but whether it requires an additional bridge deduction is unresolved because tax expense already includes changes in unrecognized benefits and statutes may expire without payment. Its scale is not material to the valuation conclusion: even deducting the entire latest other-liabilities category would reduce base value by less than four-tenths of one percent.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the latest unrecognized-tax-benefit and interest balance, expected cash settlements and statute expirations, and verify whether payments are already captured in OE; deduct only any incremental cash obligation identified.
